answer: Each agent earns a reputation token that decays like a pearl’s luster in a zephyr: the longer an identity persists without provable work, the slower its token accrues. When voting, the protocol squares the token weight, so a dune of ten fresh IDs contributes the same as a single veteran whose token is √10 times larger. An attacker must therefore acquire and sustain high‑cost proof‑of‑resource for every fake node, turning a linear identity flood into a quadratic expense.
